item.title: Commercial textile-to-textile recycling in Europe
item.description: Circulose will restart commercial textile-to-textile recycling in Sweden in late 2026. The move tests a demand-linked production model in a European market shaped by evolving EU textile policy and infrastructure constraints.

item.title: France stabilise textile EPR as resale markets weaken
item.description: France has temporarily increased financial support for textile collection and sorting under its Extended Producer Responsibility scheme, raising payments from around €228 to €268 per tonne. The €40 uplift is intended to prevent insolvencies in a sector under mounting economic pressure.

item.title: Second-hand textile exports in EU and Basel policy debates
item.description: EU waste shipment rules and Basel Convention debates are placing second-hand textile exports at the centre of textile policy. But most environmental impacts occur earlier in the production chain.

item.title: Evidence behind environmental claims in second-hand clothing trade
item.description: Debatten om miljöeffekterna av global second-hand-handel växer snabbt i takt med nya exportregler och policyförslag. Men hur stark är egentligen evidensen bakom antagandet att handeln driver miljöproblem i mottagarländer?

item.title: EU ban on destroying unsold clothing raises capacity questions
item.description: The EU ban on destroying unsold clothing is intended to reduce textile waste. But with recycling capacity still limited and reuse markets under pressure, the policy raises new questions about where surplus garments will go.

item.title: Europe’s circular textile economy faces a growing surplus
item.description: Europe is collecting more textiles than ever before as new textile policies take effect. But recycling capacity, second-hand markets and export channels are under pressure. The result is a growing surplus of clothing inside Europe’s textile system.

item.title: Recycling Europe warns EU proposal could weaken EPR enforcement
item.description: A proposal linked to the European Commission’s Environmental Omnibus initiative has triggered concerns among recycling industry representatives about the future enforcement of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) rules.

item.title: EU launches infringement case over waste directive implementation
item.description: The European Commission has launched a new infringement procedure against Lithuania for failing to properly transpose the EU’s Waste Framework Directive into national law.

item.title: EU Ecodesign rules on unsold clothing lack data
item.description: EU’s Ecodesign regulation will ban destruction of unsold clothing and introduce reporting requirements. But limited data on surplus flows leaves key system effects uncertain.

item.title: Environmental Omnibus and EU textile policy under pressure
item.description: What actually happens to the clothes that are never sold? Each year, hundreds of thousands of tonnes of garments fail to find a buyer in Europe. Most are redistributed through secondary markets. But a smaller share simply disappears from view — with limited data on where it goes or how it is handled.
